newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters clears way for changes to super plan.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters clears way for changes to super plan.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters on Thursday cleared the way for the team of officials designing a compulsory superannuation scheme to put aside elements of New Zealand First's policy.

"The design team has taken an open approach to looking at all options ... having regard to those contained in the Todd Taskforce report (on private provision for retirement) and New Zealand First policy," Peters said.

"We are not going to second guess an attempt to put together the best scheme possible. Some things that we have said may be omitted. Some things we have said may not be practical, but then again this design team might find very well that the policy we have laid out is the right policy for the country."
A core group of officials, including a private sector individual, will design the scheme to be put to a postal referendum in September.
Peters said he welcomed all submissions on the scheme.

A scheme to make everyone contribute a portion of income to an individual pension savings scheme -- initially three percent in 1998/99, rising to eight percent by 2002 -- was championed by New Zealand First and opposed by National during last year's election campaign.
The government has said it would consider itself bound by the result of the referendum.
